title: Dynamic epigenetic changes during antidepressant pharmacotherapy in major depressive disorder
title_zh: 抗抑郁药治疗中主要抑郁障碍的动态表观遗传变化
abstract: Abstract Although antidepressants remain the main pharmacological treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD), therapeutic response varies, highlighting the need for molecular markers that predict treatment response, as well as insights into the biological processes underlying antidepressant efficacy. Candidate-gene and cross-sectional epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) have reported DNA methylation signatures associated with antidepressant response; however, findings remain inconsistent. To date, no longitudinal EWAS has examined methylation trajectories across multiple time points during antidepressant treatment in MDD. Within the Early Medication Change trial, DNA methylation data was generated for 162 patients with MDD (81 responders, 81 non-responders) and 48 matched healthy controls. Patients were assessed at four times across eight-weeks of standardized antidepressant treatment, while controls were assessed twice. Differentially methylated positions (DMPs) and regions (DMRs) were identified using longitudinal EWAS models and the comb-p algorithm. Baseline methylation levels were associated with depressive symptom severity at day 28 and day 56 through two and six DMRs, respectively (e.g., TNRC6C , CAT ), whereas no single DMP reached significance. Longitudinal analyses identified one DMP associated with improvement in depressive symptoms ( YLMP1 ) and three DMRs showing methylation changes over time (e.g., GPR126, PM20D1) . Combined patient-control analyses revealed additional DMPs and DMRs associated with diagnosis and temporal effects. This study provides first longitudinal evidence of regionally coordinated DNA methylation changes during antidepressant pharmacotherapy, revealing alterations in genes involved in neuroplasticity and inflammatory processes that are associated with clinical response. Replication and functional validation will be essential to determine their relevance for personalized antidepressant treatment.
abstract_zh: 摘要 虽然抗抑郁药仍是主要抑郁障碍（MDD）的药物治疗手段，但治疗反应存在个体差异，这凸显了需要预测治疗反应的分子标志物，以及了解抗抑郁药疗效背后的生物学过程。候选基因和横断面表观基因组关联研究（EWAS）已报道了与抗抑郁药反应相关的DNA甲基化特征；然而，研究结果仍不一致。迄今为止，尚无纵向EWAS在抗抑郁治疗的多个时间点上检查MDD患者的甲基化轨迹。在早期药物转换试验中，针对162例MDD患者（81名缓解者，81名非缓解者）和48名匹配的健康对照者生成了DNA甲基化数据。患者在标准化抗抑郁治疗的8周内，于4个时间点进行评估，而对照组则评估2次。利用纵向EWAS模型和comb-p算法鉴定出了差异甲基化位点（DMPs）和区域（DMRs）。基线甲基化水平通过2个DMRs（如TNRC6C、CAT）在日28日和日56分别与抑郁症状严重程度相关，未发现单个DMP达到显著性。纵向分析确定了1个与抑郁症状改善相关的DMP（YLMP1），以及3个显示随时间甲基化变化的DMRs（如GPR126、PM20D1）。患者与对照组的联合分析揭示了与诊断和时间效应相关的额外DMPs和DMRs。本研究提供了抗抑郁药物治疗期间区域协调DNA甲基化变化的首次纵向证据，揭示了与临床反应相关的神经可塑性和炎症相关基因的改变。复制和功能验证对于确定其在个体化抗抑郁治疗中的相关性至关重要。
